title: How a Boring Podcast Got Millions of Downloads & Built a Media Empire
promo_conflict: Catherine promotes Nothing Much Happens, its books and audiobook, the upcoming app, and its website; no paid sponsor conflict is stated.

stated_problem.quote: I just kept thinking, so many people are struggling with this.

idea.name: Nothing Much Happens sleep-story media business
idea.one_liner: Original sleep-story podcasts for people seeking rest and comfort, monetized through advertising, premium subscriptions and books, with video and an app extending the brand.
idea.customer: Listeners seeking help falling asleep or a sense of comfort and companionship; advertisers and book buyers are secondary customers.
idea.offer: Free spoken sleep stories and related meditation shows, plus an ad-free membership with bonus episodes, books and video versions.
idea.revenue_model: Podcast advertising and sponsorships, optional ad-free subscriptions, book and audiobook sales or royalties; the app is in development and no app price is stated.

claims.claim: The host estimates that $40 per year from the stated subscriber base would mean more than half a million dollars in revenue.
claims.quote: At $40 a year, that's over half a million dollars in revenue, not even counting any of the other income streams.

claims.claim: Catherine says the show had about 400 episodes after six years.
claims.quote: And we launched about a month and a half later, and that was 400 episodes six years ago.

claims.claim: In the first months, Catherine says the show reached 150 downloads and then 200 downloads in a day.
claims.quote: So even when, you know, in the first couple of months, I'd get 150 downloads, and then I got 200 downloads in a day.

claims.claim: Catherine recalls daily downloads rising from 200 and 300 to 1,400 and then 3,000.
claims.quote: So I remember there was a day where, you know, it was like 200 downloads, 300 downloads, and then it was like 1400 downloads in a day, and then it was like 3,000 downloads in a day,

claims.claim: Catherine says 90% of podcasts do not get past episode 10.
claims.quote: And even if it seems crowded today, the truth is 90% of podcasts don't make it past episode 10.

claims.claim: The show had reached 10 million downloads about a year after launch.
claims.quote: About a year in, we had already hit 10 million downloads, and I came back to the idea.

claims.claim: The business spent no money on marketing until around the prior year.
claims.quote: We didn't spend a dollar on marketing until like last year.

claims.claim: Catherine recalls 600 people from Brazil commenting on the show's YouTube channel.
claims.quote: all of a sudden, 600 people from Brazil are leaving comments on my YouTube

claims.claim: The book sold in 35 countries.
claims.quote: It's sold in 35 countries, which for a first time author, which is amazing.

claims.claim: Catherine says she released a show every other week at one point.
claims.quote: I was, I think I released a show every other week.

claims.claim: Catherine says she later released two shows a week and had three podcasts.
claims.quote: And now I release like two shows a week and I have three podcasts.

claims.claim: The show began making money around 2020.
claims.quote: It's a 2020, it's probably when we started to actually make money.

claims.claim: The host describes the ad-free premium version as five dollars a month.
claims.quote: The other revenue stream is the premium subscription for the year, five bucks a month for the ad free version, plus what else is behind them?

claims.claim: The membership includes about 60 or more monthly bonus episodes.
claims.quote: Yeah, they get, or monthly bonus episodes of which now they're, I think, are about 60 or more.

claims.claim: Some bonus episodes run up to 10 hours.
claims.quote: They're sometimes up to 10 hours long.

claims.claim: The membership covers three shows without ads.
claims.quote: Everything is ad free, not just for nothing much happens, but for all three shows, stories from the village of nothing much, and first this, my meditation podcast.

claims.claim: Catherine describes the membership as costing about a dime a day.
claims.quote: So for like a dime a day, I feel like it's a pretty good value.

claims.claim: The membership launched around 2021 or 2022.
claims.quote: We launched the membership probably in 2021 or 2022.

claims.claim: Catherine reports more than 13,000 to 14,000 subscribers.
claims.quote: I think we're north of 13,000, 14,000 subscribers right now.

claims.claim: Catherine says 97% to 98% of members renew.
claims.quote: Like 97 to 98% of the people who buy a membership will renew their membership.

claims.claim: Catherine wrote a seven-episode story series.
claims.quote: I wrote a like a seven episode series about a wedding that took place in the village of nothing much.

claims.claim: Her usual stories run about 30 to 35 minutes.
claims.quote: But usually my stories are right about 30, 35 minutes.

claims.claim: It takes Catherine two weeks to write a month's worth of shows.
claims.quote: It usually takes me two weeks to write a month's worth.

claims.claim: The YouTube channel grew to about 20,000 subscribers before the team focused on it.
claims.quote: without noticing suddenly there were like 20,000 subscribers

claims.claim: The new audiobook features eight voice actors in addition to Catherine.
claims.quote: It's me and eight wonderful voice actors from Broadway, from movies and TV.
